PC: Summarizes the treatment plan for the acute problem(s) and makes clear transition statement to discuss CPR
Provides a clear summary of a plan of care and treatment for this hospitalization based on the decisions reached, and clarifies the family’s understanding of the plan
GET TO KNOW YOUR PATIENT – what are his/her values and goals?  What is meaningful in his or her life?
Ask patient or family what his/her/their understanding is of chronic medical problem(s) including prognosis
MK: Clearly reviews the patient’s current and overall medical condition and prognosis
Explores and explains the expected functional outcomes if CPR is attempted in the setting of a cardiac arrest
Makes a recommendation in light of identified goals and expected outcomes if a cardiac arrest occurred
Fill in gaps in understanding of chronic disease and clarifies prognosis
SBP: Assesses readiness to make a decision. If the patient or surrogate needed more time, establishes a decision process in terms of what to do and when to conclude the process and make a decision
ICS: Establishes a comfortable atmosphere and puts patient/family at ease
Uses understandable language and avoids medical jargon
Responds to verbal and non-verbal cues
Demonstrates empathy and compassion throughout the encounter
Ask patient/family if they have questions or concerns regarding chronic disease/prognosis
Finish by asking if the patient has any questions
PROF: Affirms the intention to provide the best care of the patient regardless of the patient’s resuscitation status
